title: I'm building my dream fantasy MMORPG with Claude Code. Would you actually play something like this?
author: Efficient-Accident96
selftext:
I've always loved games like MapleStory, Diablo and MU Online, so I decided to see how far I could get building my own fantasy RPG with AI.

I'm using Claude Code with Phaser and TypeScript, as well as AI tools for artwork, character sprites, animations and audio.

My approach is to develop in stages, playtest each iteration myself and give Claude detailed feedback. Getting consistent character animations, satisfying combat and proper hit reactions has been much more challenging than building the basic game mechanics.

The long-term vision for Vaelqora Online is an MMORPG where you can explore with friends, discover secrets, fight bosses, collect rare gear, unlock wings, pets and mounts, build your own home or simply hang out with other players.

What you're seeing is very early gameplay and it still needs loads of polishing. Multiplayer and most of the social features are planned for the future.

Before investing a lot more time into this, I'm curious what people think of the concept. Would you actually play something like this?

Happy to answer questions about the development process as well!

I've also built a website with more about the vision and future plans: [https://www.playvaelqora.com](https://playvaelqora.com)

comments.author: Professor_Snipe
comments.body: Don't make mmorpgs unless you have an audience. Even if the game is decent, there is no way for you to sustain an audience to keep playing it. Unless it's just a fun exercise for yourself, make it a grindy single player game with fun progression.

replies.author: Efficient-Accident96
replies.body: You're right! I think MMORPG might not be the right term for what I have in mind. I want it to be a fun single player RPG with cozy elements, but with the option to play with friends, explore together and meet other players along the way. It shouldn't depend on having a large playerbase to be enjoyable.

comments.author: adolphite
comments.body: The wolf you are striking looks like a pet.

replies.author: Efficient-Accident96
replies.body: Definitely one of my biggest inspirations! But I'd love to combine that style of gameplay and progression with more exploration, housing and cozy elements.

comments.author: chrisvdmeer
comments.body: Would love a maplestory like game but make it singleplayer

replies.author: Efficient-Accident96
replies.body: That's pretty much what I'm aiming for, with the option to play with friends if you want to. What did you enjoy most about MapleStory?

replies.author: chrisvdmeer
replies.body: Art style , things to explore, the different classes and powers. The feeling of getting your first class, by leveling up and traveling to a class's master

replies.author: Efficient-Accident96
replies.body: Yeah I loved that too! Especially starting out as a novice and working towards your first class. I really want progression to feel rewarding, not just through levels and stats but also through exploration, discovering new abilities and finding rare equipment.

comments.author: AnOrdinaryCrayon725
comments.body: I like how its looking as its an early stage but no, i wouldnt play it.

replies.author: Efficient-Accident96
replies.body: Thanks! Is it the type of game that doesn't appeal to you or something about the gameplay itself? Just curious!

replies.author: AnOrdinaryCrayon725
replies.body: Both. I dont like these dungeon crawler type of games and secondly the animations are very clunky. perhaps you could approach a hybrid approach to animation, using some human editing and mostly ai

replies.author: Efficient-Accident96
replies.body: I think MMORPG was the wrong term to use haha. The focus is on singleplayer, exploration, progression and cozy elements, with the option to play online and adventure with friends.

replies.author: AdStreet4350
replies.body: How can you be mistaken about your own game?

replies.author: Efficient-Accident96
replies.body: Not mistaken about the game, just how I described it. It's still early in development and part of sharing it here is to get feedback and see what resonates with people.

comments.author: Efficient-Accident96
comments.body: Small clarification after reading some of the comments. I think MMORPG is the wrong term for what I have in mind. It's primarily a single player fantasy RPG with cozy elements, but with the option to play online, meet other players and adventure with friends. You should be able to enjoy everything the game has to offer without having to play with others.

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
...I'll be honest:  I would not even try this. 

The AI visuals are too bland and uninteresting. It's the most generic fantasy art direction ever, and when I see that it immediately triggers an assumption for me that you really don't care about the work and don't really have a vision, because if you did then you'd make that apparent with the art (AI generated or otherwise).

replies.author: Efficient-Accident96
replies.body: Thanks, this is great feedback! I'm still figuring out the visual identity of the game. I personally like the art style, but I agree it needs more of its own identity.

replies.author: AsparagusOk8818
replies.body:
...It's not the art style per se, which could be fine (ish) if it had good direction.

Just as the most clear example: There is no apparent consideration of geography or context. In the scene you show, the character appear to be running along the top of some sort of rock wall or fortification... and that's where people have set-up their shops?  It looks like that's supposed to be some kind of rocky road, but that's not what you could get the AI to draw, so you shrugged and just plopped a town square onto a wall.

And the desired narrative set-up here is supposed to be a world full of adventure or whatever... but look the background landscape. Open fields and a big windmill and little communities just happily sitting out in the open.

If this is a world of adventure with monsters and wilderness and danger, with an untamed landscape, that makes no sense.

The costuming is related to this. The featured characters have no sense of personality or style. He's got generic armour; she's got generic robes. The late-game flight is enabled by generic angelic wings or generic fairy wings. Nothing feels like it belongs in a cohesive world.

Like, there's that crystal stuff everywhere. Wouldn't people be trying to mine that and make stuff out of it, instead of quarrying rock or smithing metal? People tend to exploit available resources. Why are there still so many surface deposits, especially in a world with the kind of extensive settlement shown? Why are there still so many trees nestled against the buildings that haven't been turned into timber? Why is there a fckn windmill next to a river instead of a watermill? Why does the river bisect an inhabited landscape and there's no bridge or dam? Why are the shops all burning lantern fuel in the middle of the day?

Etc, etc

EDIT: And it's not that I don't think there could be plausible answers to those questions, but rather that I suspect the real answer to literally all of those questions is, 'that's just how the AI drew it', which is what I mean about lack of art direction.

replies.author: Efficient-Accident96
replies.body: This is actually really helpful feedback. I hadn't considered some of these details from that perspective. I've been focusing heavily on combat and visuals, but you're right that the world itself needs more thought and consistency. Thanks for taking the time to explain it.

comments.author: Nattya_
comments.body: Ai games all look mostly the same and have the same idea. What makes people want to play is art direction and interesting gameplay. Something that hasnt been done a million times

replies.author: Efficient-Accident96
replies.body: I agree, making a good looking game isn't enough. It needs something that makes people actually want to keep playing. Still a lot to figure out there!

comments.author: headWw
comments.body: Honestly, it could be much worse. I kinda like the bassic attacks on the knight and its animations. The meteor on the wizard looks really bad tho same for the skills of the last boss, take some time to do some actual improvements there. Make it single-player, with some nice systems that keeps the player grinding and better/less-clunkier skills/animations. I also like the website, good job.

replies.author: Efficient-Accident96
replies.body: Thanks, really appreciate the detailed feedback! The warrior is definitely further along than the mage in terms of combat and animations. I also love games where grinding actually feels rewarding. What kind of progression systems do you enjoy most?

comments.author: YouHave24Hours
comments.body: Never ever, sorry, and that's not even because it's all AI made (yuk). Even if AI didn't do everything for you, there's a trillion games like this, and a billion good ones and a million great ones and a few masterpieces. Why would your generic, soulless, AI made and bland looking game ever be taken into consideration? Sorry to ve harsh but games worth our time, energy and money are games with soul, intent, character and originality, factors that take way way way waaaaay more than just "hey Claude, make game.here's some  reference images the other AI made for me". Have fun doing stuff (still i can not understand having "fun" giving promts while an AI copy and pastes you a crude mix of existing stuff)... You'll never have the amazing feeling of "achievement", "overcome struggles" and the satisfying feeling of "original creation" if you simply use AI for it all. Go downvote me, you'll eventually start to feel empty and dettached using AI for everything (been there).

replies.author: Efficient-Accident96
replies.body: I actually really enjoy building this, but I understand your point about originality. It's still very early in development and there's a lot of work to be done. That's also why I'm sharing it now rather than spending another year building something nobody wants to play. Thanks for the feedback!

replies.author: YouHave24Hours
replies.body: Again, there's nothing wrong IF you enjoy something by doing so... I am from a very long background of VFX/CGI/directing and ofc. me/we too dug into AI but at the end of the day - and here even most PRO-Ai would agree if they're honest - most of what people do (not "create", that's the machine) with AI looks, feels and tastes the same.. text, images, video, sound and now more and more games: 99% it all feels "seen before, dull, unnecessarily polished" and after all 99% without soul, passion and uniqueness.  Plus yeah, all i see of AI "devs" (lol) are mmorpg (aka walking demos), roguelike deckbuilders, generic scifi military/extraction shooters... there's an infinite amount already which are great in this. So, if ever, I would not touch any tool/AI before I don't have a clear vision and original idea, not just "the same looking sightly different". I feel AI makes people extremely lazy to even skip the most basic parts of creation. that's my 5 cents. again, whatever gives you joy and doesn't hurt anyone (well, generative AI hurts artists, creators, coders...) go for it. cheers!

replies.author: Efficient-Accident96
replies.body: I get your point. A good-looking game doesn't necessarily make a good game. Finding its own identity is exactly what I'm working on right now. I'm enjoying the process and learning a lot along the way. Let's see where it goes!
